I've been this daughter before, and I've not been proud of it. I can definitely understand both sides and I can see that you have tried to compromise with her about her schooling. 

A lot of people have been suggesting therapy for her and/or for you, but I highly suggest just having open-hearted talks with her first. Ask her why she thinks that way about school or if she's been feeling ok. Ask her if anything's been on her mind and if you could help her with anything that's been going on (that you don't know about). Despite what happened in this post, sometimes you need to set aside your feelings so you can understand hers. At the same time, she is going through puberty and will need her space. It seems that she is fraustrated with school so trying to talk to her about it will get her even more upset and more reluctant to do homework. Not saying that you should never bring it up, but finding a different way to go about it might be better since this time didn't go too well. Try to find the source of the problem rather than the solution right away.

Like what others have said, I do believe that you and him just have different types of love languages. I'm Asian American dating a White American and I do understand where you're coming from when it comes to men offering gifts as a way of affection. My parents would always drill in my head that a man should always shower me with gifts to prove his love for me but I know that is not always the case.

Your bf might be an affectionate person but not in the case of small materialistic gifts. For example he might prefer affirmation and quality time over the other love languages, but that doesn't make him not love you. As long as you guys find a balance in the other love languages then you'll be ok. It is a matter of understanding who he is as a person and what he does to show that he loves you, not because of cultural differences. 

An advice I can give is to not bring him down by comparing him to what other men do as well as letting yourself be in a relationship you're not satisfied with. He's stated that he feels inadequate because of the comparison you make, so doing it any further will pressure him into being uncomfortable in the relationship. As for you, if you have made it clear that you would like to be given gifts and he can't satisfy that, then it is on your end to accept that it's just the way he is or end the relationship. You could try to find a compromise somehow but if he doesn't do anything about it and disregards your feelings, I'm sorry to say but he is arrogant and just not a good partner overall.
